root_cause_label: Infinite Repetitive Command Loop After Search Failure
one_sentence_failure_summary: After failing to locate the kernel source in 28 exploratory steps, the model entered a degenerate infinite loop repeating 'ls -la /var/lib/python/' for 1159 consecutive steps, never attempting to download the source or make any progress on the task.
t_err_evidence: Step 29 is the first occurrence of 'ls -la /var/lib/python/', a command entirely irrelevant to finding or downloading the Linux 6.9 kernel source; the agent had already established (steps 1-28) that no kernel source existed in the environment, but instead of pivoting to download it, the model began generating the same useless directory listing repeatedly.
t_commit_evidence: By step 34 the alternating variation (steps 30, 32 tried '/var/lib/python3.12/') ceased and the loop became purely uniform 'ls -la /var/lib/python/' with no deviation through step 1189, locking in failure with certainty.
t_surface_evidence: Step 31 is the first step where an observer can see the agent repeating the same command ('ls -la /var/lib/python/') it already ran at step 29, providing an observable signal that the agent is stuck in a loop rather than making forward progress.
trigger_explanation: The model's generation fell into a degenerate repetitive loop: having exhausted its exploratory heuristics without finding the kernel source, the model failed to generate a qualitatively different action (e.g., wget/curl to download linux-6.9 tarball) and instead produced the same 'ls -la /var/lib/python/' command 1159 times. This is a model-level generation failure where the context led to a pathological fixed point.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 3 and 14 returned 'ramfs directory not found' and 'linux-6.9 directory not found' respectively, signaling the environment had no pre-staged kernel source. Steps 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 15, 16 all returned empty output from find commands looking for kernel files, collectively showing the agent's search strategy was failing before the loop began.
